didYouKnow.hook: Charizard is card 4 of 102 because of the alphabet.
didYouKnow.body: The English Base Set was ordered by card type first, then by how rare the card was, then alphabetically by name. Among the holo rares that put Alakazam at 1, Blastoise at 2, Chansey at 3 — and Charizard at 4.
didYouKnow.why_it_matters: So the most recognisable number in the hobby, 4/102, is not a designation of importance. It is where the letter C landed.
sources: Bulbapedia: Base Set (TCG) — English release ordering
Bill's Archive: Base Set complete guide

sealedIndex.name: Catchem Sealed Index
sealedIndex.baseline: Chain-linked. A name joins on the first day it has a price and does not move the level that day. Its first return is the next day it is priced. Each day's move is the trimmed geometric mean of price changes of names priced on both days: each change is capped at 30% down or 43% up, and the top and bottom 10% are dropped when 10 or more names are priced. A value-weighted line gives a dearer product a bigger say. A day with no shared prices is a gap. Nothing is filled in.
sealedIndex.simple: One number for the whole sealed market. It starts at 100 and moves by the average daily change of the products we track — only products we could price on both days count toward a move, so adding or removing products never shifts it.

valueWeighted.name: Catchem Sealed Index — value weighted
valueWeighted.simple: Same shelf, but the expensive boxes get a bigger say. If this number and the main one disagree, the cheap end and the expensive end of the market are moving differently.
valueWeighted.method: Each product's move is weighted by what it was worth at its baseline, so a $5,000 box counts for more than a $10 pack. The main index gives every product one equal vote.

model.formula: buyerCeiling = ask × (1 + taxPct/100) · sellerFloor = ask × (1 − feePct/100) − feeFixed
